user_identity_reconciliation.note: old_user_id == new_user_id for all 354 rows; this is one shared users table read through two codebases, not two populations that happen to match

pending_migration_count_discrepancy_note: An earlier document in this repo (supabase-new-details.md) reported 16 pending migrations. Recounted fresh via `supabase migration list` three times this phase and independently recounted by two separate sub-audits: the correct figure is 18. The earlier '16' figure should be treated as superseded by this document.

pending_migrations.note: updates stage_no/order on 5 existing live stage rows (STG007-STG011, +2 shift, display fields only, no FK impact); creates STG012/STG013 stage rows and 12 chapter shells
only touches CH0117/CH0118, both created in this same pending batch

pending_migrations.known_issue: missing 'enable row level security' statement; must be added before/with deployment

curriculum_mapping_note: OLD and NEW use identical STGnnn/CHnnnn IDs; every shared chapter/stage is IDENTICAL_ID (see migration/curriculum-compatibility-report.md). No ID translation table is needed. NEW_ONLY additions (STG012, STG013, CH0116, CH0117-CH0128) are pure additions with no OLD equivalent to map from.
progress_migration_note: No migration needed: OLD and NEW read/write the same live learn_progress/test_runs/attempts rows. Zero existing progress references STG007-STG011 or STG012/STG013 (confirmed: those stages have zero recorded student activity live). Applying the pending curriculum migrations creates no orphaned references.
xp_migration_note: The XP pipeline (pending_xp/committed_xp, partial-unique-index-gated single commit per chapter) is byte-identical shared code, already live, already governing all 354 users' current total_xp. Two known pre-existing data characteristics (43 completed_repeat runs with non-zero historical XP; 2 of 354 accounts with a total_xp/derived-sum mismatch) are not caused by and not affected by the pending migrations, and should not be 'corrected' as part of this work.
hearts_migration_note: Hearts logic is byte-identical shared code. None of the 18 pending migrations touch users.hearts or heart_recovery fields.
auth_note: Auth code (SHA-256(salt|password) hashing, random-UUID session tokens, requireSession idle-timeout check) is byte-identical between OLD and NEW. No Supabase Auth/auth.users usage in either repo. Since both repos run the identical auth code against the same live users/sessions tables, existing students already authenticate identically through either codebase -- no credential migration or hash-scheme decision is required.
edge_function_diff_summary: CRLF-tolerant multi-line answer comparison (bugfix, NEW only)
completeLearn message wording differs only when unified flag is set (NEW only)
startTest gains a 'unified' chapter mode (NEW only, caps questions via settings.UNIFIED_MAX_QUESTIONS)
finishTest auto-completes learn_progress for unified runs (NEW only)
finishTest message wording differs for unified vs non-unified (NEW only)
database_writes_note: Only read-only operations were performed: projects list, link (local config only), migration list, inspect db index-stats/table-stats. No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/ALTER/CREATE/DROP of any kind.
unresolved_items: Live MD5 set-hash fingerprint evidence for the same-database claim (from the OLD-side audit) was not independently re-run by this phase; all other angles of evidence are independently confirmed and consistent with it.

2,173 (test_runs.committed_xp sum, completed-only) vs 1,873 (attempts.xp_earned sum, completed-only) -- a ~300-unit gap between two related XP metrics in the OLD-side audit package that is not reconciled anywhere in that package. Flagged, not resolved, by this phase.
The 2 specific accounts with an XP reconciliation mismatch are intentionally not identified (to avoid exposing which students) -- would require a fresh live query to locate.

Exact live row-content reconciliation for the 115-row chapters table (which specific rows, beyond the aggregate counts) was confirmed via cross-referencing both repos' independent audits rather than a single direct live SELECT, since no general-purpose read query tool (psql/pg_dump, both requiring Docker, unavailable in this environment) was available this phase.
